notes: Catalog of Hunspell dictionaries smaragd hosts and can download on request (Settings > Spell Check > Dictionaries, src/spellcheck.rs, GitHub issue #47). This file itself is compiled into the smaragd binary (include_str!), but each entry's actual dictionary files live in a separate repo, https://github.com/ljantzen/smaragd-dictionaries/<language_code>/, each with its own SOURCE (exact upstream commit pinned, never a moving branch) and LICENSE (the upstream license text, verbatim) -- see that repo's README.md for the full explanation of why redistributing a non-GPL or even GPL-2.0-only dictionary is fine (GPLv2's own 'mere aggregation' allowance: these stay independent, unmodified, un-linked data files, never compiled or linked into the application). `redistributable`/`review_status` reflect this project's own reading of the upstream license/README files at the pinned commit, not a legal opinion for any other use case.

dictionary_source_policy.description: Only individually reviewed dictionary artifacts -- pinned to an exact upstream commit, with their license text preserved verbatim and their copyright holder identified -- are distributed. A dictionary whose review_status starts with "blocked" is never offered for download regardless of what its own license technically permits.
dictionary_source_policy.license_isolation: Every dictionary is kept as a genuinely separate, unmodified file (own LICENSE/SOURCE, never compiled or linked into smaragd's own source or binary) so its license never applies to smaragd's own code, and smaragd's GPL-3.0-or-later never applies to it.

dictionaries.review_status_notes: Same SCOWL/VarCon project and license terms as en_US (Kevin Atkinson's permissive word-list grant plus the Ispell-derived BSD-style affix file) -- this is the "-ise" spelling variant, the standard British form. wooorm/dictionaries' own package.json independently classifies this exact file as "(MIT AND BSD)", matching en_US. The .aff file is in fact byte-identical to en_US.aff: SCOWL/VarCon shares its affix rules across English locale variants, only the word list differs.

dictionaries.review_status_notes: Freely selectable triple-license scheme (GPL-2.0 / LGPL-2.1 / MPL-1.1), per wooorm/dictionaries' own package.json SPDX expression, corroborated by this dictionary's own bundled LICENSE text listing exactly the same three options -- same pattern as es_ES/pt_PT in this catalog. Recorded under GPL-2.0-only (no "or later" stated for that option); redistributed as a genuinely separate data file under GPLv2's own mere-aggregation allowance, same reasoning as nb_NO/nn_NO/pt_PT. Unlike every other entry in this catalog, index.dic here is NOT byte-identical to upstream: 4 of the original 173,515 entries failed to parse under standard Hunspell dic syntax (an upstream Stavekontrolden data bug, confirmed still present in their latest 2.8.116 release, not a wooorm packaging issue or something a newer pin would fix). 3 unescaped-slash abbreviations ("A/S", "c/o", "I/S") were fixed by escaping the slash per Hunspell's own dic-format convention -- same word, now parseable. 1 corrupted entry (two dictionary lines concatenated without a line break) was ambiguous to reconstruct and was deleted outright rather than guessed at. Full accounting in da_DK/SOURCE.
